content: Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect calculation of the maximum allocation size for memory regions in the Intel graphics driver. The original implementation limited the maximum allocation size based on the `mm.max_order`, which represents the largest power-of-two that can fit within the region size. However, this approach did not account for scenarios where the memory region size is not a power-of-two (e.g., 3G). As a result, allocations that should have been valid were incorrectly rejected, leading to allocation failures. The patch corrects this by ensuring that the maximum allocation size is based on the actual size of the memory region instead of the power-of-two limitation.

Code statements:
```c
-	if (size > BIT(mem->mm.max_order) * mem->mm.chunk_size)
+	if (size > mem->mm.size)
```
